answer: A sybil-resistant design is stake-weighted mutual attestation: a new identity only becomes active after several established agents vouch for its real work, each staking part of their own reputation and funds. If the vouched identity cheats, its vouchers are slashed too, so spinning up a plume of clones costs the attacker real collateral each time. Clone clusters also leave an umber trail in the attestation graph, dense reciprocal links unlike organic trust, and honest agents act as a reef, refusing to vouch for identities with no verified history.
